34 Which statement about the electromotive force (e.m.f.) of a cell is always correct?
A
The e.m.f. is the energy converted from electrical to other forms in the cell.
B
The e.m.f. is the energy provided by the cell per unit charge passing through it.
C
The e.m.f. is the potential difference across the internal resistance of the cell.
D
The e.m.f. is the potential difference across the terminals of the cell.

hints: Focus on the word always and test each statement for open-circuit versus closed-circuit conditions with current $I$ and internal resistance $r$.
Recall the defining relation $E = W/Q$ for e.m.f., where $W$ is energy supplied by the cell and $Q$ is charge passing through it.
Compare that definition with $V = E - Ir$ for the terminals and $Ir$ for the internal resistance to see which statement has no exceptions.
walkthrough: Note the question asks for the statement that is always true, so a statement true only on open circuit or only with current cannot be correct.
State the governing definition: e.m.f. is the energy transferred from non-electrical to electrical form per unit charge driven through the cell, $E = W/Q$.
Check the energy direction: the cell supplies energy, so any statement saying electrical energy is converted to other forms inside the cell contradicts the source action.
Check the internal resistance: the p.d. across it is $Ir$, the lost volts, which is zero when $I = 0$ and only part of $E$ when $I > 0$.
Check the terminals: terminal p.d. is $V = E - Ir$, so $V = E$ only when $I = 0$ and $V < E$ when current flows.
Only the energy provided per unit charge statement holds in all cases with correct units of $\text{J C}^{-1}$. This is option B.

A.explanation: Reversed energy direction - the cell converts chemical or other energy to electrical energy, not electrical to other forms.

B.explanation: Matches the definition $E = W/Q$, the work done by the cell per unit charge in $\text{J C}^{-1}$ or volts.

C.explanation: The p.d. across internal resistance is only the lost volts $Ir$, which is just part of the e.m.f. when current flows.

D.explanation: Terminal p.d. $V = E - Ir$ equals $E$ only on open circuit, so it is not always equal to e.m.f.
